newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end higher as correction halted.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end higher as correction halted.

text.p: Swiss shares closed one percent higher in modest volume, putting an end to a three-day downward correction.
But activity was described as low as many investors were seen sidelined ahead of U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's economic report to Congress later in the day and on Wednesday.
"The market was more or less dead," one dealer said.
The Swiss environment for stocks was seen as favourable as recent economic data made interest rate hikes seem unlikely.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 56.6 points, or 1.01 percent, at 5,677.1. The day's high was reached at 5,713.8.
"The market may move between 5,650 and 5,800 SMI points this week," one trader said.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 33.64 points, or 0.94 percent, to 3,606.20.
Bourse volume was at 2.49 billion Swiss francs.
One dealer added the firming dollar brightened sentiment.
The market was also helped by a technical reaction to recent losses, which were partially due to derivatives-linked selling.
During the afternoon, some profit taking led to a slip below 5,700 SMI points again.
Most-active Novartis added 17 francs to 2,309. The company is expected to release favourable first half-year sales on Thursday, one dealer said.
Banks were seen rebounding from a period of weakness.
CS Group added three francs to 192.50. One trader said that Monday's merger of Germany's fourth- and fith-largest banks did not have much of an impact on Swiss banks.
Specialty chemicals firm Clariant rose 51 francs to 1,005.
Clariant may report a 20 percent rise in first half-year sales on Wednesday, one dealer said.
Nestle and Surveillance, considered some of the most dollar-sensitive stocks on the Swiss bourse, underperformed the market.
"I would expect these shares to show bigger gains given the strong dollar," one dealer said.
Nestle ended 10 francs higher at 1,875.
One of the winners of the day was Swiss Life, which jumped 51 francs to 676 on buys by a Geneva-based bank, dealers said.
